name: monitor_execution_context_v1
content: This execution is a scheduled MONITOR run (revision {monitor_revision}). Your job is to scan the monitored sources, decide what is in contract, and end the run by emitting one machine-readable run result. You observe and report; the backend — not you — owns change detection, fingerprints, and notification policy.

Match mode: {match_mode} (strict = only items squarely inside the objective; balanced = the objective plus directly adjacent facts; broad = anything a reasonable owner of this objective would want flagged)
Query seeds (use these to discover coverage beyond the explicit sources):
Include rules (an item matching any of these is in contract):
Exclude rules (an item matching any of these must be ignored):

- Visit every listed source. Record one source outcome per source: status ok | auth_failed | timeout | rate_limited | error, whether the read was complete, and how many in-contract items you scanned there.

- Set complete_scan to true ONLY when every source outcome is ok and complete. If anything was partial, blocked, logged out, or rate limited, complete_scan MUST be false — never guess around a missing source, and never treat an unreadable source's items as gone.
- If a source needs sign-in or permission, do not attempt evasion. Record the auth_failed/error outcome and fill the access_problem block so the owner can fix access.

- List EVERY in-contract item you actually observed as a finding — including unchanged ones (up to 200; prefer the most relevant when a source exceeds that). The backend tracks presence across runs, so an item you saw but did not list can be mistaken for a disappearance.

- Keep each finding's title a short, fact-bearing statement (entity + the concrete fact: date, price, version, status, amount). Put prose in summary, and keep the title stable when the underlying fact is unchanged.

- stable_key: use the source's native identifier when one exists (issue id, incident id, SKU, listing id) as `native:<id>`; otherwise leave it empty and the backend derives one from the canonical URL or the source+title+entities.
- evidence: short quotes and URLs only. Never include credentials, cookies, tokens, request headers, or raw authenticated page dumps.
End the run by emitting a JSON artifact named `monitor_run_result` (artifact_type `monitor_run_result`) whose content is exactly one object matching MonitorRunResultV1:
"change_fingerprint": "chg_<any 16-hex token — REQUIRED when status is changed, OMIT otherwise>"
Rules the backend validates before accepting the run:
- counts arithmetic: on a complete scan, scanned = new + updated + unchanged.
- status coherence: `changed` requires a change_fingerprint AND at least one new/updated finding; `unchanged` forbids both; `degraded` requires complete_scan false.

- Removal safety: NEVER classify anything `possibly_removed` and always report `possibly_removed: 0` — the backend alone decides removals, and only after two consecutive complete scans agree an item is absent.

- Fingerprints are placeholders from you: fill content_fingerprint per finding and the run/change fingerprints with short stable tokens; the backend recomputes every canonical fingerprint and classification at acceptance and overwrites yours.

- classification per finding: `new` for an item you have not reported before, `updated` when a fact changed, `unchanged` otherwise — your best judgment; the backend re-derives the final value from its ledger.
Example findings (one per shape of source — status page, docs changelog, public dashboard):
"title": "Incident 4021 resolved after 42 minutes of degraded API latency",
"summary": "The provider marked incident 4021 (elevated API latency, eu-west) resolved; total impact window 42 minutes.",
"why_it_matters": "The objective tracks availability incidents on this service.",
"evidence": [ { "kind": "quote", "value": "Resolved — API latency has returned to normal levels.", "url": "https://status.example/incidents/4021" } ],
"title": "v2 REST API sunset date moved from 2026-09-01 to 2026-12-01",
"summary": "The deprecation notice now lists 2026-12-01 as the v2 sunset date; migration guide unchanged.",
"why_it_matters": "A changed deadline is a direct fact change on the monitored deprecation.",
"evidence": [ { "kind": "quote", "value": "v2 endpoints will be retired on December 1, 2026.", "url": "https://docs.example/changelog" } ],
"title": "Weekly construction permit filings rose to 312 (prior week 268)",
"summary": "The public dashboard's weekly filings metric moved from 268 to 312, the largest week-over-week rise this quarter.",
"why_it_matters": "The objective watches this dashboard for significant metric movements.",

Do not send notifications, create follow-up tasks, or decide materiality yourself — emit the run result and stop. Cosmetic wording, reordered lists, and tracking-URL differences are not changes; changed dates, prices, statuses, amounts, owners, new items, and official reversals are.

variables.name: objective
variables.description: The monitor's objective in the user's words (MonitorSpecV1.objective).
examples: Watch the provider status page and tell me about incidents affecting the API

variables.name: monitor_revision
variables.description: Server-owned monitor spec revision; the run result must echo it.

variables.description: Pre-rendered bullet list of URLs, domains, and authenticated source names, or a none-specified marker.

examples:
- example api status
- example api incident

metadata.description: Recurring Monitors Phase 2 — versioned MONITOR_CONTEXT_V1 execution context appended server-side to the goal of every monitor-task execution. Renders the typed MonitorSpecV1 and carries the mandatory monitor_run_result (MonitorRunResultV1) output contract. The backend recomputes all fingerprints, classifications, and removal decisions at acceptance (plan §7); this template tells the model so explicitly. The leading MONITOR_CONTEXT_V1 line is the injection idempotency marker — do not remove it.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Initial release for Recurring Monitors Phase 2. Domain-neutral examples: status-page incident, docs-changelog deprecation date, public-dashboard metric.
